ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Cars A and B are on the same horizontal road, one in front of the other separated by x=4 m, with car B in front and car A behind. At a certain moment the two cars start moving at the same time. According to the x-t graph shown in the figure, how does the velocity of car B change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an x-t graph, with the vertical axis labeled x/m and the horizontal axis labeled t/s. The graph line labeled “B” is a curve that bends downward to the right and descends, with position x decreasing as time t increases; moreover, from left to right the curve descends more and more steeply, the tangent slope is negative, and the absolute value of the slope gradually becomes larger. Reasoning: In an x-t graph, the tangent slope of the graph line represents velocity. The slope of car B's graph line is negative, indicating that car B moves in the direction of decreasing x; the absolute value of the slope continuously increases, indicating that the magnitude of car B's velocity continuously increases.
